tagline: Leading financial services provider for growing businesses and families
hero_kpi_rationale: Net income is the primary indicator of the bank's overall financial performance, reflecting its ability to generate profits from operations, investments, and services.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Net Income — bottom-line profit after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income increased by 18% in 2025 compared to 2024, reaching $7.0 billion.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total revenues increased 7% in 2025 to reach $23.1 billion.

kpis.name: Net Interest Income
kpis.explanation: Net Interest income generated over the period.
kpis.description: Net interest income increased by 7% in 2025, reaching $14.4 billion, driven by lower funding costs and the repricing of fixed-rate assets.

kpis.name: Noninterest Income
kpis.explanation: Noninterest income generated over the period.
kpis.description: Non-interest revenues increased by 8% in 2025 to reach $8.7 billion, driven by capital markets, fees, and asset management.

kpis.name: Efficiency Ratio
kpis.description: The efficiency ratio improved to 60% in 2025, down from 63% in 2024, indicating better cost management.

kpis.name: Provision for credit losses
kpis.explanation: Amount set aside to cover potential losses on loans and other receivables.
kpis.description: The allowance for credit losses was $779 million in 2025, slightly below $789 million in 2024.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.explanation: Total Assets — sum of all assets on the balance sheet.
kpis.description: Total assets increased by 2.4% to reach $573.6 billion at the end of 2025.

kpis.name: Total Deposits
kpis.explanation: Total amount of customer deposits held by the bank.
kpis.description: Total deposits increased by 3.3% to reach $440.9 billion at the end of 2025.

kpis.name: Common equity tier 1
kpis.explanation: The most stringent capital ratio, measuring the bank's ability to absorb losses.
kpis.description: The Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio stood at 10.6% at the end of 2025, slightly up from 10.5% in 2024.

stories_kpis.name: FDIC Special Assessment Release
stories_kpis.explanation: Release of provisions following FDIC's downward revision of expected banking losses.
stories_kpis.description: In 2025, PNC benefited from a release of provisions of $108 million related to the FDIC special assessment, following a revision of expected losses (60M in Q4 and 48M in Q3).
stories_kpis.signal: Significant reduction in expenses related to the special FDIC assessment in 2025, benefit of $108 million.

stories_kpis.name: Visa Exchange Program Gain
stories_kpis.explanation: Exceptional gain realized from the conversion of Visa Class B-1 shares into Visa Class B-2 and Class C shares.
stories_kpis.description: In the second quarter of 2024, PNC realized a $754 million gain from the conversion of its Visa Class B-1 shares into Visa Class C shares, while retaining the Class B-2 shares.
stories_kpis.signal: Significant exceptional gain of $754 million related to the Visa exchange program in Q2 2024.

stories_kpis.name: Investment Securities Portfolio Repositioning Loss
stories_kpis.explanation: Accounting loss incurred from the sale of low-yielding securities to reinvest in higher-yielding securities.
stories_kpis.description: In the second quarter of 2024, PNC recorded a $497 million loss on the repositioning of its investment securities portfolio, selling $3.8 billion of low-yielding securities and redeploying the proceeds into higher-yielding securities.
stories_kpis.signal: Accounting loss of $497 million related to a portfolio optimization strategy in Q2 2024.

ai_positioning.summary: The company PNC does not have significant mentions of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar technologies in the provided excerpts. Its positioning on this topic is therefore not identifiable from this information.

risks.title: Deterioration in loan portfolio quality
risks.summary: Deterioration in economic conditions or borrower risk profiles could increase loan defaults and credit losses.
risks.score_rationale: Risk is central in the 10-K, with explicit mention of the impact of economic conditions on credit losses. The language emphasizes uncertainty in economic forecasts (real GDP, unemployment) and the use of probabilistic scenarios, indicating high risk. Compared to the prior year, the focus on macroeconomic forecasts intensifies its severity. The Credit category is heavily weighted for a bank.

risks.title: Dependence on economic forecasts for credit losses
risks.summary: Loan loss estimates are highly dependent on uncertain economic forecasts, which may affect the reliability of the ACL.
risks.score_rationale: The document details the use of four weighted macroeconomic scenarios, centered on real GDP and unemployment rate. The level of management judgment is described as 'significant' by the auditor, increasing the risk of error. This factor is repeated in the 'Critical Audit Matters', indicating heightened importance compared to the prior year.

risks.title: Use of qualitative reserves in the ACL
risks.summary: Subjective adjustments in the allowance for loan losses could bias the assessment of actual risks and impact capital strength.
risks.score_rationale: Qualitative reserves are noted as reflecting losses not captured by models. Their subjective nature is emphasized by the auditor, who had to engage experts. This risk is stable but critical as it affects transparency and capital robustness.

risks.title: Concentration sectorielle et conditions industrielles
risks.summary: Significant exposure to distressed sectors could increase credit losses.
risks.score_rationale: Risk is cited as a qualitative factor in the ACL. Although important, it is mentioned generically without specific concentration data. The language is cautious but not alarming. Less central than macro or credit risks.

risks.title: Limitations of rating models and input data
risks.summary: Credit risk models may be imperfect due to incomplete data or methodological biases.
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly cites 'limitations of available data' and 'imprecision of models' as qualitative factors. This reflects a structural modeling risk, but without indication of a current deficiency. Less critical category for a traditional bank.

governance.voting_structure_note: Single class of common stock, 1 vote per share.
